text: The museum opens at nine in the morning. Before the visitors arrive, Maya checks the lights in the exhibition rooms and unlocks the side door for the cleaning staff. A school group has booked a guided tour at ten. Their teacher wants the children to compare old maps with a modern street plan. Some roads have kept their names for hundreds of years, while others disappeared when the railway station was built. Maya lays a transparent sheet over the old map so the children can trace the river and find the bridge. They discover that the river once followed a wider bend through the present market square. This helps explain why several streets turn at an unusual angle. At the end of the tour, each child sketches a route from the station to the museum and labels three landmarks. The teacher collects the drawings to discuss them in class the next day.

Ania pracuje w niewielkiej pracowni ceramicznej. Rano przygotowuje glinę, sprawdza wilgotność i zapisuje numer partii. Każde naczynie schnie powoli na drewnianej półce. Jeśli wyschnie zbyt szybko, na powierzchni mogą pojawić się pęknięcia. Po pierwszym wypaleniu Ania nakłada szkliwo i odkłada kubki do ponownego wypalenia. Kolor przed wypaleniem nie zawsze odpowiada kolorowi gotowego wyrobu. Dlatego przy każdej nowej mieszance wykonuje małą próbkę. Klient zamówił sześć niebieskich kubków i dwa białe talerze. Zamówienie ma być gotowe w piątek. Ania sprawdza harmonogram pieca, żeby wszystkie elementy zdążyły ostygnąć przed pakowaniem. Na kartonie zapisuje nazwisko klienta oraz liczbę sztuk. Do środka wkłada instrukcję mycia naczyń i kartkę z podziękowaniem.

A cache stores results of expensive computations. The key must include every input that changes the result. If the computation also depends on a configuration version, that version belongs in the key. A simple Python implementation uses a dictionary:

def square_cached(value, cache):
    if value not in cache:
        cache[value] = value * value
    return cache[value]

cache = {}
assert square_cached(7, cache) == 49
assert square_cached(-3, cache) == 9
assert square_cached(7, cache) == 49
assert len(cache) == 2

This example needs no eviction policy because the input set is small. A long-running service may receive millions of distinct inputs. It needs a memory limit and a policy for removing entries. The least recently used policy keeps track of access order. Tests should verify both the returned values and the behavior when the limit is reached.

A telescope collects light over an interval of time. A longer exposure reveals faint stars, but the camera also records more noise. Astronomers take several exposures and combine them after aligning the images. They use dark frames to estimate the sensor's background signal and flat frames to correct uneven sensitivity. The calibration images must match the observing conditions closely enough to be useful. If the telescope moves during an exposure, stars appear as short streaks rather than points. Tracking software adjusts the mount to compensate for the rotation of the Earth. The observer checks a nearby guide star and corrects small deviations. After processing, the final image can show details that were difficult to see in any single exposure. A careful analysis still records the exposure times, the filters used, and the uncertainty of the measurements. A visually attractive picture is not by itself a measurement of a star's brightness.

A garden has eight rows of plants, with twelve plants in each row. There are ninety-six plants in total. If each plant needs half a litre of water, one watering uses forty-eight litres. A tank containing two hundred and forty litres supplies five complete waterings. The gardener waters on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. After those three waterings, ninety-six litres remain in the tank. These numbers assume that no water is lost through evaporation or leaks. In practice, the gardener checks the level rather than relying only on the calculation. A second garden has six rows with ten plants per row. It contains sixty plants and needs thirty litres for each watering. Together, the two gardens require seventy-eight litres. Dividing the available volume by this requirement gives the number of possible combined waterings. The result must be rounded down when only complete waterings are counted.

Start with two or three herbs you use regularly. Put taller plants toward the back so they do not shade shorter ones. Choose pots with drainage holes and place trays underneath to protect the balcony floor. Check the soil before watering: the surface may look dry while the roots still have enough moisture. Label each pot, especially when the plants are young. Leave enough space to reach every pot comfortably. You can group herbs with similar watering needs together. Basil usually needs more frequent attention than rosemary. Watch the plants during the first week and adjust their positions if the afternoon sun is too strong. A little observation helps more than following a fixed watering schedule.
